scope: Specific reusable AKS procedures suggested by current guides and recurring question patterns. No frequency ranking or efficacy claim. Community answers supply symptoms, not authoritative repair rules.

candidates.question: How many outbound IPs and per-node ports do we need at maximum scale, including upgrades?
candidates.missing_procedure: Round per-node ports to eight, include all pool maxima and approved concurrent surge, size 64000-port frontends and update the AKS owner rather than its reconciled LB.
candidates.negative_control: Fit current nodes only or edit generated outbound rule.

candidates.question: Why does custom DNS work directly or briefly but not persist through normal pod resolution?
candidates.missing_procedure: Use coredns-custom import suffixes, preserve main/legacy config, reload and verify affected plus preserved query paths.
candidates.negative_control: Edit managed Corefile, use an unimported suffix, omit process reload or verify only direct upstream.

candidates.question: Can this existing PVC grow beyond 4 TiB without downtime?
candidates.missing_procedure: Branch on actual disk SKU, detach when required, grow existing claim, restore consumer and verify mounted filesystem/data without recreation.
candidates.negative_control: Treat all disk types as online or take unnecessary downtime for Premium v2.

candidates.question: Does our vault configuration really protect every PV against regional failure?
candidates.missing_procedure: Join PV driver/class and disk size/access/DES fields; separate Operational/Vault tier, paired-region restore and secondary RPO.
candidates.negative_control: Call every CSI volume eligible, conflate four-hour snapshots with Vault RPO or weaken security to pass eligibility.

candidates.question: Why is the pod subnet full when visible pod IP use looks low?
candidates.missing_procedure: Separate node/pod subnets; account for per-node 16-address allocations, refill below eight free, surge and churn before comparing NNC allocations to apparent demand.
candidates.negative_control: Use Overlay /24-per-node arithmetic or count only Running pods.

candidates.question: Why does one pool's upgrade fail for another subnet?
candidates.missing_procedure: Inventory every pool/subnet, distinguish CNI modes, use applicable maxima and surge, account for reserved/other addresses, and select an authorized feasible upgrade envelope.
candidates.negative_control: Apply legacy maxPods formula to Overlay or inspect only the upgraded pool.

candidates.question: How do we migrate in-tree volumes without creating empty replacement disks?
candidates.missing_procedure: Set Retain before logical object removal; preserve physical disk handle, prebind replacement CSI PV/PVC and verify data/consumer continuity.
candidates.negative_control: Delete a Delete-policy claim first or create an unrelated dynamically provisioned disk.

candidates.question: Can we recover a Released retained PV after a claim was accidentally deleted?
candidates.missing_procedure: Verify Retain and disk/data identity, resolve the old claim reservation, explicitly bind the new claim and verify content without deleting the physical asset.
candidates.negative_control: Assume same claim name means same UID or permit a default class to provision new storage.

candidates.question: Is a ReadyToUse disk snapshot enough to recover the database consistently?
candidates.missing_procedure: Quiesce writes using the application's supported protocol, snapshot the correct volume, restore a new consumer and validate application/data consistency rather than snapshot metadata alone.
candidates.negative_control: Snapshot during uncontrolled writes and declare application consistency.

candidates.question: A retained LRS disk will not attach after a zone change; should we just edit node labels?
candidates.missing_procedure: Compare actual disk zone and eligible capacity; preserve truthful topology and data, choose a same-zone pool or approved storage migration instead of falsifying labels/affinity.
candidates.negative_control: Relabel a physical zone or remove PV affinity to pretend cross-zone LRS attachment works.

candidates.question: Why do idle nodes remain after lowering the autoscaler maximum?
candidates.missing_procedure: Use requests/allocatable rather than CPU usage alone; inspect move feasibility, PDB/safe-to-evict/local storage and timers; distinguish scale-up cap from scale-down eligibility.
candidates.negative_control: Force node deletion or assume maxCount enforces unconditional shrink.

candidates.question: HPA reports missing CPU requests although the application container has them; why?
candidates.missing_procedure: Inspect admitted pod and every container, including injected sidecars, then distinguish resource metric denominator problems from provider/RBAC errors.
candidates.negative_control: Reinstall metrics-server or increase node capacity without checking actual container requests.

candidates.question: Why are Spot pools ignored even with a priority expander?
candidates.missing_procedure: Verify exact group-name regex coverage, priority ordering and fallback eligibility using current pool identities rather than copying ambiguous sample priorities.
candidates.negative_control: Reverse higher/lower priority or leave the intended node group unmatched.

candidates.question: Are unhealthy LB backends evidence of broken nodes when externalTrafficPolicy is Local?
candidates.missing_procedure: Join ready local endpoint placement, healthCheckNodePort and Azure probe behavior; distinguish expected nonserving-node probe failure from a real probe/path fault without losing source IP.
candidates.negative_control: Switch to Cluster just to make probes green or declare every nonlocal node broken.

candidates.question: Why did enabling Private Link PROXY protocol break otherwise healthy Local-service probes?
candidates.missing_procedure: Check PROXY-header support of the actual health endpoint, distinguish kube-proxy health port from app probes and configure an authorized compatible probe/receiver pair.
candidates.negative_control: Assume Local /healthz supports PROXY headers or change direct managed-LB configuration.

candidates.question: Can we extend service address capacity without recreating a supported cluster?
candidates.missing_procedure: Gate on supported version/allocator and address plan; add ServiceCIDR, preserve existing IPAddress ownership and verify new allocation; distinguish extension from moving the original service range.
candidates.negative_control: Mutate immutable original range or delete a range still containing live service IPs.

candidates.question: Can we move to NAT Gateway without breaking API access or external allowlists?
candidates.missing_procedure: Use actual managed/BYO migration matrix, associate required egress resources, update allowlists/authorized IPs and plan disruption/verification before cutover.
candidates.negative_control: Assume public egress IP is preserved or choose a managed-VNet-only mode on BYO networking.

candidates.question: A supported recovery point exists, so why does target restore validation fail?
candidates.missing_procedure: Separate extension identity, vault identity, trusted access, target/snapshot/staging scopes and restore-tier roles; validate before starting and preserve security constraints.
candidates.negative_control: Grant subscription Owner or repeatedly restart restore without checking its named principal/scope.

candidates.question: Why does a successful live patch revert, and how do we make the repair durable?
candidates.missing_procedure: Trace field ownership to Flux source/path, modify the approved repository overlay, reconcile and verify revision; restore any authorized temporary suspension and avoid prune-driven data loss.
candidates.negative_control: Leave reconciliation suspended or edit only live resources.

candidates.question: Deployments are blocked by a webhook; can we recover without globally disabling enforcement?
candidates.missing_procedure: Read matched webhook rules, service endpoints, TLS and tunnel evidence, then restore the failing relationship or use an explicitly approved narrow exception with rollback.
candidates.negative_control: Set every failurePolicy to Ignore or assume a healthy pod proves API-server reachability.

candidates.question: Which certificate failed, and would rotating the cluster CA cause avoidable downtime?
candidates.missing_procedure: Distinguish serving/client/CA identities, inspect actual expiry/signer/rotation state and choose supported component-specific action; do not approve arbitrary CSRs or rotate the whole cluster blindly.
candidates.negative_control: Disable TLS verification or treat every x509 error as expired cluster CA.

candidates.question: Why can our old Azure Linux pool no longer scale even though Kubernetes still runs?
candidates.missing_procedure: Pin retirement dates and supported OS/Kubernetes/FIPS matrix; distinguish node-image refresh from OS SKU migration, stage workload validation and preserve rollback feasibility.
candidates.negative_control: Assume a node-image-only update necessarily moves to a supported OS major version.

candidates.question: Why does Azure Files still fail after its Kubernetes secret was updated?
candidates.missing_procedure: Classify DNS/TCP445 versus SMB auth/cipher failure, verify key version without disclosing it and resolve stale mount/consumer lifecycle through an approved remount path.
candidates.negative_control: Rotate working credentials for a network timeout or declare success from Secret metadata alone.

candidates.question: A new routing object exists but traffic still reaches the old controller; what is missing?
candidates.missing_procedure: Identify actual ingress/Gateway ownership, listener/parent attachment and backend readiness, preserve old routes and verify hostname/TLS/path before authorized DNS cutover.
candidates.negative_control: Delete existing routing or switch DNS based only on resource creation.
